claim: The 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif is a cis-regulatory RNA element located immediately downstream of the 7-methylguanosine [m7G] cap of TOP mRNAs.
source: The 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif is a cis-regulatory RNA element located immediately downstream of the 7-methylguanosine [m7G] cap of TOP mRNAs, which encode ribosomal proteins and translation factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the 5'TOP motif structure and location.

claim: TOP mRNAs encode ribosomal proteins and translation factors.
source: The 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif is a cis-regulatory RNA element located immediately downstream of the 7-methylguanosine [m7G] cap of TOP mRNAs, which encode ribosomal proteins and translation factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about what TOP mRNAs encode.

claim: The 5'TOP motif coordinates the synchronous and stoichiometric expression of the protein components of the translation machinery in eukaryotes.
source: In eukaryotes, this motif coordinates the synchronous and stoichiometric expression of the protein components of the translation machinery.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of the 5'TOP motif.

claim: La-related protein 1 (LARP1) binds TOP mRNAs.
source: La-related protein 1 (LARP1) binds TOP mRNAs, regulating their stability and translation.
evidence: This is supported by prior research cited in the manuscript.

claim: LARP1 regulates the stability and translation of TOP mRNAs.
source: La-related protein 1 (LARP1) binds TOP mRNAs, regulating their stability and translation.
evidence: This is supported by prior research cited in the manuscript.

claim: The crystal structure of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with a 5'TOP motif was resolved to 2.6 Å.
source: We present crystal structures of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with a 5'TOP motif, a cap analog (m7GTP), and a capped cytidine (m7GpppC), resolved to 2.6, 1.8 and 1.7 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is directly reported experimental data from the study.

claim: The crystal structure of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with m7GTP was resolved to 1.8 Å.
source: We present crystal structures of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with a 5'TOP motif, a cap analog (m7GTP), and a capped cytidine (m7GpppC), resolved to 2.6, 1.8 and 1.7 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is directly reported experimental data from the study.

claim: The crystal structure of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with m7GpppC was resolved to 1.7 Å.
source: We present crystal structures of the human LARP1 DM15 region in complex with a 5'TOP motif, a cap analog (m7GTP), and a capped cytidine (m7GpppC), resolved to 2.6, 1.8 and 1.7 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is directly reported experimental data from the study.

claim: LARP1 directly binds the cap and adjacent 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs.
source: We show that LARP1 directly binds the cap and adjacent 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs, effectively impeding access of eIF4E to the cap and preventing eIF4F assembly.
evidence: This is supported by the crystallographic and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: LARP1 impedes access of eIF4E to the cap of TOP mRNAs.
source: We show that LARP1 directly binds the cap and adjacent 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs, effectively impeding access of eIF4E to the cap and preventing eIF4F assembly.
evidence: This is supported by competition assays and immunoprecipitation data.

claim: LARP1 prevents eIF4F assembly on TOP mRNAs.
source: We show that LARP1 directly binds the cap and adjacent 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs, effectively impeding access of eIF4E to the cap and preventing eIF4F assembly.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data showing reduced eIF4G association with TOP mRNAs.

claim: LARP1 is a specialized TOP mRNA cap-binding protein that controls ribosome biogenesis.
source: Thus, LARP1 is a specialized TOP mRNA cap-binding protein that controls ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented.

claim: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins carry a 5'TOP motif.
source: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins, most translation factors, and some RNA-binding proteins carry a cis-regulatory RNA element termed the 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif comprising an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides and preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap (Fonseca et al., 2014; Iadevaia et al., 2008; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Most translation factors carry a 5'TOP motif.
source: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins, most translation factors, and some RNA-binding proteins carry a cis-regulatory RNA element termed the 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif comprising an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides and preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap (Fonseca et al., 2014; Iadevaia et al., 2008; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Some RNA-binding proteins carry a 5'TOP motif.
source: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins, most translation factors, and some RNA-binding proteins carry a cis-regulatory RNA element termed the 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif comprising an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides and preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap (Fonseca et al., 2014; Iadevaia et al., 2008; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The 5'TOP motif comprises an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides.
source: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins, most translation factors, and some RNA-binding proteins carry a cis-regulatory RNA element termed the 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif comprising an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides and preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap (Fonseca et al., 2014; Iadevaia et al., 2008; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is the established definition of the 5'TOP motif supported by citations.

claim: The 5'TOP motif is preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap.
source: All transcripts encoding ribosomal proteins, most translation factors, and some RNA-binding proteins carry a cis-regulatory RNA element termed the 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif comprising an invariant 5'-cytidine followed by an uninterrupted tract of 4–14 pyrimidine nucleotides and preceded by the 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7Gppp) cap (Fonseca et al., 2014; Iadevaia et al., 2008; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is the established definition of the 5'TOP motif supported by citations.

claim: The 5'TOP motif is essential for translation regulation of TOP mRNAs.
source: This motif is essential for translation regulation of TOP mRNAs (Biberman and Meyuhas, 1999; Avni et al., 1994; Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling pathway plays a prominent role in the control of TOP mRNA translation.
source: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling pathway plays a prominent role in the control of TOP mRNA translation (Fonseca et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2012; Thoreen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: mTORC1 boosts the production of components of the translation machinery encoded by TOP mRNAs in response to provision of nutrients.
source: In response to provision of nutrients (such as amino acids, growth factors, glucose, or oxygen), the growth-associated kinase complex mTORC1 boosts the production of components of the translation machinery encoded by TOP mRNAs (Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015; Chantranupong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of mTORC1 results in the pronounced repression of TOP mRNA translation.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of mTORC1 results in the pronounced repression of TOP mRNA translation (Terada et al., 1994; Jefferies et al., 1994; Thoreen et al., 2012; Hsieh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: TOP mRNAs are the class of transcripts that are most sensitive to translation suppression by mTOR inhibitors.
source: Genome-wide ribosome profiling studies demonstrate that TOP mRNAs are the class of transcripts that are most sensitive to translation suppression by mTOR inhibitors (Thoreen et al., 2012; Hsieh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to genome-wide ribosome profiling studies.

claim: eIF4E and its repressor proteins, 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2, have been linked to the control of TOP mRNA translation downstream of mTORC1.
source: Most recently, the mRNA cap-binding protein, eIF4E, and its repressor proteins, 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2, have been linked to the control of TOP mRNA translation downstream of mTORC1 (Hsieh et al., 2012; Thoreen, 2017; Thoreen et al., 2012), but the exact contribution of 4E-BPs to the control of TOP mRNA translation remains a point of contention (Miloslavski et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The exact contribution of 4E-BPs to the control of TOP mRNA translation remains a point of contention.
source: Most recently, the mRNA cap-binding protein, eIF4E, and its repressor proteins, 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2, have been linked to the control of TOP mRNA translation downstream of mTORC1 (Hsieh et al., 2012; Thoreen, 2017; Thoreen et al., 2012), but the exact contribution of 4E-BPs to the control of TOP mRNA translation remains a point of contention (Miloslavski et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation indicating disagreement in the field.

claim: LARP1 was identified as a novel downstream target of mTORC1.
source: Recently, we and others (Fonseca et al., 2015; Tcherkezian et al., 2014) identified La-related protein 1 (LARP1) as a novel downstream target of mTORC1 and proposed that it plays an important role in the translation of TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors and others.

claim: LARP1 plays an important role in the translation of TOP mRNAs.
source: Recently, we and others (Fonseca et al., 2015; Tcherkezian et al., 2014) identified La-related protein 1 (LARP1) as a novel downstream target of mTORC1 and proposed that it plays an important role in the translation of TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors and others.

claim: LARP1 associates with the regulatory-associated protein of mTOR (RAPTOR) when mTORC1 is active.
source: Specifically, we have shown that LARP1 associates with the regulatory-associated protein of mTOR (RAPTOR) when mTORC1 is active.
evidence: This is supported by prior research by the authors.

claim: Upon mTORC1 inhibition, LARP1 dissociates from mTORC1 and binds to the 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs.
source: Upon mTORC1 inhibition, a cellular state that is associated with TOP mRNA translation repression, we demonstrated that LARP1 dissociates from mTORC1 and binds to the 5'TOP motif of TOP mRNAs (Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by prior research by the authors.

claim: LARP1 associates with the 5'TOP motif via a LARP1 family-specific 'DM15 region' located within its C-terminus.
source: We have also shown that LARP1 associates with the 5'TOP motif via a LARP1 family-specific 'DM15 region' located within its C-terminus (Lahr et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by prior research by the authors.

claim: There is a direct association between the DM15 region and the 5'TOP motif.
source: In the present study, we confirm a direct association between the DM15 region and the 5'TOP motif.
evidence: This is confirmed by the crystallographic and biochemical data in the present study.

claim: The DM15 region of LARP1 specifically binds the 7-methylguanosine 5'−5' triphosphate (m7Gppp) moiety and the invariant first cytidine of TOP mRNAs.
source: We show that the DM15 region of LARP1 specifically binds the 7-methylguanosine 5'−5' triphosphate (m7Gppp) moiety and the invariant first cytidine of TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by the crystal structures and biochemical assays presented.

claim: LARP1 selectively prevents the binding of eIF4E to the m7Gppp cap to block the assembly of the eIF4F complex on TOP mRNAs.
source: Biochemical analyses reveal that LARP1 selectively prevents the binding of eIF4E to the m7Gppp cap to block the assembly of the eIF4F complex on TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by competition assays and immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: m7GTP binds the same pocket as G8* in the DM15-RNA co-crystal.
source: To test this, we determined the co-crystal structure of DM15 bound to the cap analog 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7GTP) to 1.8 Å resolution. m7GTP binds the same pocket as G8* in the DM15-RNA co-crystal (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structures shown in Figure 1C and supplements.

claim: Lysine-915 stabilizes the γ-phosphate of m7GTP.
source: Lysine-915 stabilizes the γ-phosphate of m7GTP (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Residues from each of the conserved DM15 repeats (A, B, C) participate in the recognition of the invariant cytidine in the first position of TOP mRNAs (C1) and the guanosine (G8*) 5' to it.
source: Residues from each of the conserved DM15 repeats (A, B, C) participate in the recognition of the invariant cytidine in the first position of TOP mRNAs (C1) and the guanosine (G8*) 5' to it (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structures shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: All of the amino acids that interact directly with the RNA are nearly 100% conserved from worms to mammals and plants.
source: All of the amino acids that interact directly with the RNA are nearly 100% conserved from worms to mammals and plants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) (Bousquet-Antonelli and Deragon, 2009; Lahr et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and citations.

claim: Amino acids R840, R879, and H800 define the path of the RNA by aligning it on the surface of DM15 through ionic and hydrogen bonding interactions with the phosphate backbone.
source: Amino acids R840, R879, and H800 define the path of the RNA by aligning it on the surface of DM15 through ionic and hydrogen bonding interactions with the phosphate backbone.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Amino acids Y922, Y883, and F844 stabilize the nucleobases of G8* and C1 through stacking interactions.
source: Amino acids Y922, Y883, and F844 stabilize the nucleobases of G8* and C1 through stacking interactions.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Sequence-specific recognition of G8* through its Watson-Crick face is accomplished by hydrogen bonds with E886 and S882.
source: Sequence-specific recognition of G8* through its Watson-Crick face is accomplished by hydrogen bonds with E886 and S882.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Arginines 847 and 879 specifically recognize C1.
source: Arginines 847 and 879 specifically recognize C1 (Bousquet-Antonelli and Deragon, 2009; Lahr et al., 2015).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure and supported by citations.

claim: The DM15 region of LARP1 stabilizes the nucleobase of m7GTP between two conserved aromatic amino acids, Y883 and Y922.
source: The DM15 region of LARP1 stabilizes the nucleobase of m7GTP between two conserved aromatic amino acids, Y883 and Y922.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: E886 hydrogen bonds with the Watson-Crick face of the guanosine moiety.
source: In addition, E886 hydrogen bonds with the Watson-Crick face of the guanosine moiety, using acidic side chains for this recognition in a mechanism reminiscent to that of other cap-binding proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 4, CBP20).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure and compared to other cap-binding proteins.

claim: DM15 binds a 42-mer oligonucleotide of the 5'UTR of RPS6 containing an additional 5'G with an affinity of 7.5 μM.
source: DM15 binds a 42-mer oligonucleotide of the 5'UTR of RPS6 containing an additional 5'G, effectively making it a non-5'TOP sequence, with an affinity of 7.5 μM; capping this substrate enhances affinity 3.8-fold (2.0 μM).
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays.

claim: Capping the non-TOP RPS6 substrate enhances DM15 binding affinity 3.8-fold (2.0 μM).
source: DM15 binds a 42-mer oligonucleotide of the 5'UTR of RPS6 containing an additional 5'G, effectively making it a non-5'TOP sequence, with an affinity of 7.5 μM; capping this substrate enhances affinity 3.8-fold (2.0 μM).
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays.

claim: Capping the TOP 42-mer RPS6 RNA substrate increases the affinity 360-fold (21 nM) over the non-TOP substrate.
source: Capping the TOP 42-mer RPS6 RNA substrate increases the affinity 360-fold (Figure 2; 21 nM) over the non-TOP substrate and 95-fold over the capped non-TOP substrate.
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: Capping the TOP 42-mer RPS6 RNA substrate increases the affinity 95-fold over the capped non-TOP substrate.
source: Capping the TOP 42-mer RPS6 RNA substrate increases the affinity 360-fold (Figure 2; 21 nM) over the non-TOP substrate and 95-fold over the capped non-TOP substrate.
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mutating E886 in DM15 decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA 380-fold (8.0 μM).
source: Mutating the residues in DM15 that stabilize the cap, E886, Y922, or Y883, decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA 380-fold (8.0 μM), 124-fold (2.6 μM), and greater than ~950 fold (N.D.,>20 μM), respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutating Y922 in DM15 decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA 124-fold (2.6 μM).
source: Mutating the residues in DM15 that stabilize the cap, E886, Y922, or Y883, decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA 380-fold (8.0 μM), 124-fold (2.6 μM), and greater than ~950 fold (N.D.,>20 μM), respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutating Y883 in DM15 decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA greater than ~950 fold (>20 μM).
source: Mutating the residues in DM15 that stabilize the cap, E886, Y922, or Y883, decreases the affinity for capped TOP RNA 380-fold (8.0 μM), 124-fold (2.6 μM), and greater than ~950 fold (N.D.,>20 μM), respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly measured by electrophoretic mobility shift assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Capped mRNAs better displace capped DM15-bound sequences than uncapped mRNAs do.
source: Further, competition assays in which capped mRNAs better displace capped DM15-bound sequences than uncapped mRNAs do, suggest the interaction of DM15 with the cap moiety is specific (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly measured by competition assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The interaction of DM15 with m7GTP and m7GpppC is increasingly stabilizing to the DM15 fold.
source: Finally, thermal shift stability assays demonstrate the interaction of DM15 with m7GTP and m7GpppC is increasingly stabilizing to the DM15 fold (Figure 2—figure supplement 4); notably, the m7GpppG dinucleotide does not impart additional stability to DM15 over m7GTP.
evidence: This is directly measured by thermal shift assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The m7GpppG dinucleotide does not impart additional stability to DM15 over m7GTP.
source: Finally, thermal shift stability assays demonstrate the interaction of DM15 with m7GTP and m7GpppC is increasingly stabilizing to the DM15 fold (Figure 2—figure supplement 4); notably, the m7GpppG dinucleotide does not impart additional stability to DM15 over m7GTP.
evidence: This is directly measured by thermal shift assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The DM15 region of LARP1 specifically recognizes the m7GpppC motif characteristic of TOP mRNAs.
source: Together with the conservation of the residues interacting with m7GTP, the base-specific hydrogen bonding of the Watson-Crick faces of nucleobases of G8* and C1 in the DM15-RNA co-crystal structure and the recognition of the m7GpppC dinucleotide in the DM15-m7GpppC co-crystal structure, these data suggest the DM15 region of LARP1 specifically recognizes the m7GpppC motif characteristic of TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of structural and biochemical data.

claim: The first cytidine is indispensable for repression of TOP mRNA translation.
source: This observation is particularly remarkable because the first cytdine is indispensable for repression of TOP mRNA translation (Levy et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The first cytidine is essential for LARP1 association with RPS6 and RPL32 mRNAs.
source: Interestingly, the first cytidine is also essential for LARP1 association with RPS6 and RPL32 mRNAs (Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The m7GpppC motif might lock the register of DM15 binding.
source: Higher-order complexes and nonspecific binding of DM15 to the RNA oligonucleotide are greatly reduced in the capped-TOP substrate binding reaction (Figure 2), indicating that the m7GpppC motif might lock the register of DM15 binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of reduced nonspecific binding in the presence of the cap.

claim: LARP1 differentiates TOP mRNAs from all other cellular mRNAs, most of which have a purine in the +1 position.
source: Furthermore, these data provide a molecular mechanism by which LARP1 differentiates TOP mRNAs from all other cellular mRNAs, most of which have a purine in the +1 position (Schibler et al., 1977; Schibler and Perry, 1977).
evidence: This is inferred from the specificity data and supported by citations about the +1 position in other mRNAs.

claim: Most cellular mRNAs have a purine in the +1 position.
source: Furthermore, these data provide a molecular mechanism by which LARP1 differentiates TOP mRNAs from all other cellular mRNAs, most of which have a purine in the +1 position (Schibler et al., 1977; Schibler and Perry, 1977).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Displacement of DM15 from capped TOP RNA requires high-micromolar concentrations of eIF4E.
source: While displacement of DM15 from capped TOP RNA requires high-micromolar concentrations of eIF4E, low-nanomolar concentrations of DM15 are sufficient to displace eIF4E from this substrate.
evidence: This is directly measured by competition assays.

claim: Low-nanomolar concentrations of DM15 are sufficient to displace eIF4E from capped TOP RNA.
source: While displacement of DM15 from capped TOP RNA requires high-micromolar concentrations of eIF4E, low-nanomolar concentrations of DM15 are sufficient to displace eIF4E from this substrate.
evidence: This is directly measured by competition assays.

claim: eIF4E outcompetes DM15 for the non-TOP substrate as the pre-bound or competitor protein.
source: Interestingly, the opposite is true for capped non-TOP mRNA: eIF4E outcompetes DM15 for the non-TOP substrate as the pre-bound or competitor protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly measured by competition assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: eIF4E has a preferred binding for m7GpppG.
source: These results are consistent with the preferred binding of eIF4E for m7GpppG (Kiraga-Motoszko et al., 2011; Thoreen et al., 2012; et al., Tamarkin-Ben-Harush et al., 2017) and with studies suggesting that quiescent cells and translation systems contain a factor that represses TOP mRNA translation even in the presence of excess eIF4E (Shama et al., 1995; Biberman and Meyuhas, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Quiescent cells and translation systems contain a factor that represses TOP mRNA translation even in the presence of excess eIF4E.
source: These results are consistent with the preferred binding of eIF4E for m7GpppG (Kiraga-Motoszko et al., 2011; Thoreen et al., 2012; et al., Tamarkin-Ben-Harush et al., 2017) and with studies suggesting that quiescent cells and translation systems contain a factor that represses TOP mRNA translation even in the presence of excess eIF4E (Shama et al., 1995; Biberman and Meyuhas, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The affinity of the DM15 region of LARP1 for TOP mRNAs is considerably higher than that of full-length eIF4E protein for this class of mRNAs.
source: Of note, we show that the affinity of the DM15 region of LARP1 for TOP mRNAs is considerably higher than that of full-length eIF4E protein for this class of mRNAs, likely explaining why excess eIF4E alone is insufficient to upregulate the translation of TOP mRNAs (Shama et al., 1995).
evidence: This is directly measured by competition assays and supported by a citation.

claim: Excess eIF4E alone is insufficient to upregulate the translation of TOP mRNAs.
source: Of note, we show that the affinity of the DM15 region of LARP1 for TOP mRNAs is considerably higher than that of full-length eIF4E protein for this class of mRNAs, likely explaining why excess eIF4E alone is insufficient to upregulate the translation of TOP mRNAs (Shama et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The eIF4F complex has been linked to the control of TOP mRNA translation.
source: The eIF4F complex (formed by the cap-binding protein eIF4E, the scaffolding protein eIF4G and the ATP-dependent RNA helicase eIF4A) has been linked to the control of TOP mRNA translation (Thoreen et al., 2012; Hsieh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: eIF4G co-precipitates TOP mRNAs in an mTORC1–dependent manner.
source: Moreover, eIF4G co-precipitates TOP mRNAs in an mTORC1–dependent manner (Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The ability of TOP mRNAs to associate with eIF4G is markedly inhibited upon overexpression of LARP1 in mammalian cells.
source: Notably, the ability of TOP mRNAs to associate with eIF4G is markedly inhibited upon overexpression of LARP1 in mammalian cells (Fonseca et al., 2015), consistent with the idea that LARP1 competes with eIF4E and eIF4G for binding to TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Expression of wild type LARP1 hinders the binding of endogenous eIF4G to both RPS6 and RPL32 mRNAs, but not to β-actin mRNA.
source: Expression of wild type LARP1 hinders the binding of endogenous eIF4G to both RPS6 and RPL32 mRNAs, but not to β-actin mRNA, as determined by RNA-immunoprecipitation/RT-ddPCR (Figure 3).
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-immunoprecipitation/RT-ddPCR shown in Figure 3.

claim: LARP1 binds to the cap and 5'TOP sequence of TOP mRNAs, thus selectively inhibiting eIF4F assembly on this class of transcripts.
source: This finding is consistent with the model that LARP1 binds to the cap and 5'TOP sequence of TOP mRNAs, thus selectively inhibiting eIF4F assembly on this class of transcripts.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Expression of the LARP1 R840E/Y883A double mutant does not inhibit eIF4G association with TOP mRNAs.
source: Perhaps more importantly, expression of the LARP1 R840E/Y883A double mutant does not inhibit eIF4G association with TOP mRNAs (Figure 3), indicating that cap- and TOP-binding is essential for LARP1-mediated displacement of the eIF4F complex from TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-immunoprecipitation/RT-ddPCR shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cap- and TOP-binding is essential for LARP1-mediated displacement of the eIF4F complex from TOP mRNAs.
source: Perhaps more importantly, expression of the LARP1 R840E/Y883A double mutant does not inhibit eIF4G association with TOP mRNAs (Figure 3), indicating that cap- and TOP-binding is essential for LARP1-mediated displacement of the eIF4F complex from TOP mRNAs.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutant data shown in Figure 3.

claim: mTORC1 inhibition decreases the association of eIF4G with TOP transcripts.
source: Taken together with data demonstrating mTORC1 inhibition decreases the association of eIF4G with TOP transcripts (Fonseca et al., 2015), these data suggest that mTORC1 blocks the inhibitory function of LARP1.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: mTORC1 blocks the inhibitory function of LARP1.
source: Taken together with data demonstrating mTORC1 inhibition decreases the association of eIF4G with TOP transcripts (Fonseca et al., 2015), these data suggest that mTORC1 blocks the inhibitory function of LARP1.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of current and prior data.

claim: LARP1 plays a fundamental role in the specialized recognition of the m7GpppC motif.
source: The data presented in this study provide important structural insights into the molecular mechanism of LARP1, a specific 5'TOP motif-binding protein. LARP1 plays a fundamental role in the specialized recognition of the m7GpppC motif, a unique feature of TOP mRNAs that encode all the core protein components of the ribosome and the translation apparatus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented.

claim: TOP mRNAs encode all the core protein components of the ribosome and the translation apparatus.
source: The data presented in this study provide important structural insights into the molecular mechanism of LARP1, a specific 5'TOP motif-binding protein. LARP1 plays a fundamental role in the specialized recognition of the m7GpppC motif, a unique feature of TOP mRNAs that encode all the core protein components of the ribosome and the translation apparatus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TOP mRNAs.

claim: LARP1 regulates translation and stability of TOP mRNAs through specialized 5'TOP motif and cap recognition.
source: LARP1 regulates translation and stability of this class of mRNAs through specialized 5'TOP motif (Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2015; Aoki et al., 2013) and cap recognition.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research and the current study's data.

claim: LARP1 displaces eIF4E from capped TOP mRNAs, thereby preventing the assembly of the eIF4F complex required for translation initiation.
source: Our work demonstrates that LARP1 displaces eIF4E from capped TOP mRNAs, thereby preventing the assembly of the eIF4F complex required for translation initiation.
evidence: This is supported by the competition assays and immunoprecipitation data.

claim: There is a previously unrecognized mTORC1-regulated dynamic interplay between LARP1 and the eIF4F complex.
source: These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mTORC1-regulated dynamic interplay between LARP1 and the eIF4F complex, whereby eIF4F stimulates TOP mRNA translation while LARP1 represses it.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: eIF4F stimulates TOP mRNA translation while LARP1 represses it.
source: These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mTORC1-regulated dynamic interplay between LARP1 and the eIF4F complex, whereby eIF4F stimulates TOP mRNA translation while LARP1 represses it.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: LARP1 exhibits higher specificity and affinity for TOP mRNAs than eIF4E does.
source: Notably, LARP1 exhibits higher specificity and affinity for TOP mRNAs than eIF4E does, suggesting it may function as the selective factor for TOP mRNA translation regulation.
evidence: This is supported by the competition assays and binding affinity measurements.

claim: LARP1 may function as the selective factor for TOP mRNA translation regulation.
source: Notably, LARP1 exhibits higher specificity and affinity for TOP mRNAs than eIF4E does, suggesting it may function as the selective factor for TOP mRNA translation regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the specificity and affinity data.

claim: Overexpression of LARP1 in mammalian cells leads to reduced TOP mRNA translation.
source: These findings corroborate our earlier report (Fonseca et al., 2015) that LARP1 functions as a repressor of TOP mRNA translation: overexpression of LARP1 in mammalian cells leads to reduced TOP mRNA translation, as inferred by the accumulation of TOP mRNAs in subpolysomal fractions.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Depletion of LARP1 protein from mammalian cells leads to an accumulation TOP messages in heavy polysomal fractions.
source: Conversely, depletion of LARP1 protein from mammalian cells leads to an accumulation TOP messages in heavy polysomal fractions (Fonseca et al., 2015), indicating that LARP1 represses TOP mRNA translation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: LARP1 represses TOP mRNA translation.
source: Conversely, depletion of LARP1 protein from mammalian cells leads to an accumulation TOP messages in heavy polysomal fractions (Fonseca et al., 2015), indicating that LARP1 represses TOP mRNA translation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors and the current study's data.

claim: LARP1 is essential for the ability of allosteric (rapamycin) and active-site (Torin1) mTOR inhibitors to effectively suppress TOP mRNA translation.
source: Importantly, LARP1 is essential for the ability of allosteric (rapamycin) and active-site (Torin1) mTOR inhibitors to effectively suppress TOP mRNA translation (Fonseca et al., 2015), consistent with LARP1 functioning downstream of mTORC1.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: LARP1 functions downstream of mTORC1.
source: Importantly, LARP1 is essential for the ability of allosteric (rapamycin) and active-site (Torin1) mTOR inhibitors to effectively suppress TOP mRNA translation (Fonseca et al., 2015), consistent with LARP1 functioning downstream of mTORC1.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing LARP1's role in mTOR inhibitor effects.

claim: In cancer cells, LARP1 has been shown to have a positive effect on overall protein synthesis.
source: It is noteworthy that whilst LARP1 is shown here to repress TOP translation, in cancer cells LARP1 has been shown to have a positive effect on overall protein synthesis (Burrows et al., 2010) and bind many mRNA targets, including those encoding oncogenes (Hopkins et al., 2016; Mura et al., 2015), in addition to TOP mRNAs (Aoki et al., 2013; Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2015; Tcherkezian et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: LARP1 binds many mRNA targets, including those encoding oncogenes, in addition to TOP mRNAs.
source: It is noteworthy that whilst LARP1 is shown here to repress TOP translation, in cancer cells LARP1 has been shown to have a positive effect on overall protein synthesis (Burrows et al., 2010) and bind many mRNA targets, including those encoding oncogenes (Hopkins et al., 2016; Mura et al., 2015), in addition to TOP mRNAs (Aoki et al., 2013; Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2015; Tcherkezian et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: LARP1, while repressing TOP translation, can activate the translation of other targets.
source: This suggests that LARP1, while repressing TOP translation, can activate the translation of other targets, although the mechanism for the latter has yet to be elucidated.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that LARP1 has different effects on different mRNA targets.

claim: The mechanism by which LARP1 activates the translation of non-TOP targets has yet to be elucidated.
source: This suggests that LARP1, while repressing TOP translation, can activate the translation of other targets, although the mechanism for the latter has yet to be elucidated.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: LARP1 competes with eIF4E for binding the cap of TOP mRNAs, effectively preventing eIF4F complex assembly on TOP mRNAs and ultimately precluding the translation of this class of mRNAs.
source: In conclusion, our findings elucidate a novel mechanism of translation control whereby LARP1 competes with eIF4E for binding the cap of TOP mRNAs, effectively preventing eIF4F complex assembly on TOP mRNAs and ultimately precluding the translation of this class of mRNAs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the data presented in the study.

claim: LARP1 is a bona fide cap-binding protein.
source: Our studies now establish LARP1 as a bona fide cap-binding protein and the long-sought regulator of TOP mRNA translation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented.

claim: LARP1 is the long-sought regulator of TOP mRNA translation.
source: Our studies now establish LARP1 as a bona fide cap-binding protein and the long-sought regulator of TOP mRNA translation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented and the context of prior research.
